title: Наказание в больнице и мясной секрет  (Hospital Punishment and the Meat Secret)

segments.t: Returned to his hospital bed, Chef Barinov is scolded by the nurse for climbing out the window and driving his blood pressure up. When Vika arrives to visit the supposedly weak patient, she catches him happily devouring smuggled meat with a huge appetite.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Alright then, get some rest.' Max proceeds quietly right here and uses "otdykhayte" ("rest", from "otdykhat") to make the point stick.
'Get some rest. Albert Igorevich?' Following up frankly in the exchange, Sasha keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Max purely through rising pitch.
'We need to stabilize your blood pressure.' Max fires back bluntly with a shrug, leaving no doubt about where he stands.
'Climbing out the window like that.' Touching on the window during the talk, Sasha leans on "okoshko" ("little window") to give the whole sentence its punch.
'I am begging you, please.' Following up warmly before Sasha, Max keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Sasha purely through rising pitch.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
'I will check in again this evening, and right now I will bring you some tea.' Sasha replies briskly facing Max, testing Max's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
'How are things going with you?' Max jumps in candidly on the spot and chooses "dela" ("things, affairs", from the root "delo") so Sasha hears the exact meaning.
'Detained while attempting to escape.' Addressing the attempt on the spot, Sasha uses "popytke" ("attempt", from "popytka") to make the point stick.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
'I already know everything, I will come visit you.' Max reacts dryly across the room, before Sasha can change the subject.
'What should I bring you?' Sasha jumps in naturally around Max and reaches for the Russian word "privezti" ("to bring") right at the heart of the line.
'Running and jumping around.' Cutting in boldly before Sasha, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'He is eating with such an appetite.' Sasha speaks up bluntly toward Max, before Max can change the subject.
'Learn the Russian language first.' Turning to the language beside Sasha, Max centers the remark on "russkiy" ("Russian") without any extra fuss.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
That wraps up this scene as back in the hospital ward, the nurse scolds Barinov for climbing out the window while Vika discovers him wolfing down smuggled meat under his blanket. See you next time!
